back: Autarky is no trade: prices are set by domestic supply and demand. Under free trade, domestic prices converge to the world price and the country gains overall.
Absolute: can produce a good with fewer resources. Comparative: lower opportunity cost of producing it. Trade gains come from comparative advantage.

front: How do you calculate opportunity cost from hours per unit?
back: If a good needs h1 hours and another needs h2 hours per unit, the opportunity cost of one unit of good 1 is h1/h2 units of good 2.

front: Between what values must the terms of trade lie for both countries to gain?
back: Between the two countries' opportunity costs of the good. A country will not trade at a worse rate than it can get at home.

Ricardian: comparative advantage arises from differences in technology or labour productivity. Heckscher-Ohlin: it arises from differences in factor endowments; countries export goods intensive in their abundant factor.
Index of export prices / index of import prices x 100. A rise is an improvement; a fall is a deterioration.

front: Effects of a tariff in a small country
back: Domestic price rises by the tariff; consumer surplus falls; producer surplus and government revenue rise; deadweight loss from over-production and under-consumption; net national loss.
Same domestic price effect. Tariff: government captures the revenue. Quota: licence holders capture the rent. VER: foreign exporters capture the rent, so the importing country's loss is larger.
Exporters gain, domestic consumers lose, government pays, net welfare loss. A large exporter also lowers the world price and worsens its terms of trade.

front: Levels of regional economic integration (least to most)
back: Free trade area, customs union (common external tariff), common market (free movement of labour and capital), economic union (harmonised policies), monetary union (common currency).

Creation: members switch from high-cost domestic production to low-cost member imports (welfare up). Diversion: members switch from low-cost non-member imports to higher-cost member imports (welfare down).
